response: Yes, plate clearing has been identified as a potential risk factor for obesity. This behavior, also known as "cleaning one's plate," can lead to overeating and consuming more calories than needed, contributing to weight gain and obesity. Research suggests that people who consistently finish everything on their plate, regardless of their hunger level, may be more likely to develop obesity. This is because it can lead to ignoring internal hunger and fullness cues, resulting in excessive calorie intake.
